quote: The philosopher's body must also be prepared for hard work, so that virtue may not fail.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: One cannot live well today without acting rightly today.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: Luxury damages both body and mind, making men soft and incapable of labor.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: To master oneself is the greatest mastery of all.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: Eating for pleasure rather than health is the sign of a gluttonous mind.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: Hardship is the sharpening stone for human character.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: Virtue is not a theoretical science, but a practical habit of living.
author: Musonius Rufus

quote: I begin to speak only when I am certain that what I speak is not better left unsaid.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: Doing right is its own reward; fear not the judgment of the crowd.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: Patience under injustice is a shield that no weapon can pierce.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: I prefer that men ask why there is no monument to me than why there is one.
author: Cato the Younger

quote: Freedom is a possession of inestimable value, not to be surrendered for comfort.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: Control your grief, for mourning does not alter destiny.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: A man's virtue is tested when he stands alone against corrupt custom.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: He who lives uprightly fears no tyrant's wrath.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: Custom without justice is merely ancient error.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: An upright life needs no defender but its own integrity.
author: Cato the Younger
source: Plutarch, Life of Cato the Younger

quote: Fate leads the willing, but drags the unwilling.
author: Cleanthes

quote: Conduct me, O Zeus, and thou O Destiny, whithersoever I am by you appointed to go.
author: Cleanthes

quote: Ignorance is the mother of all foolish fear.
author: Cleanthes

quote: No human action is without consequence in the grand order of nature.
author: Cleanthes

quote: The wise man obeys the universal law, while the foolish man struggles against it.
author: Cleanthes

quote: Nothing takes place on earth apart from thee, Lord, nor in the divine ethereal sphere, save what the wicked do in their own folly.
author: Cleanthes

quote: Virtue is a harmony of the soul tuned to reason.
author: Cleanthes

quote: Steel your mind against pain, for it is but a transient impression.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers

quote: Happiness is a good flow of life.
author: Zeno of Citium

quote: We have two ears and one mouth, so we should listen more than we speak.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.23

quote: A friend is another self.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.23

quote: Wellbeing is attained little by little, and yet is no little thing itself.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.26

quote: Man conquereth the world by conquering himself.
author: Zeno of Citium

quote: Better to trip with the feet than with the tongue.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.26

quote: The goal of life is living in agreement with nature.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.87

quote: Extravagance is a blind waste of energy and life.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.22

quote: Grief is an irrational contraction of the soul.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.111

quote: All things are parts of one single system, which is called Nature.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.87

quote: To live in accordance with virtue is equivalent to living in accordance with experience of the actual course of nature.
author: Zeno of Citium
source: Diogenes Laërtius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers 7.88
